detail: Begin distributing vaccine to administration sites—about four months before season onset.
Start the vaccination campaign before incidence begins rising to capture as many people as possible at outpatient points of care.
Aim to reach maximum vaccine uptake before the surveillance onset threshold is crossed.
Confirm antiviral supply and distribute stock to outpatient and acute-care sites.
As community influenza activity rises, update the pre-test probability used to interpret influenza testing results and guide empiric treatment decisions.
The national curve exceeds the surveillance onset threshold.
Reinforce hand hygiene, staying home when ill, masking when appropriate, and avoiding crowded indoor exposure.
Redistribute staffing, diagnostics, pharmaceuticals, and equipment toward regions experiencing the greatest burden.
Communicate that cases may be turning while asking the public and health systems to sustain effective interventions.
Early vaccine-effectiveness estimates become available after most vaccination-timing decisions are already complete.
Select the Northern Hemisphere vaccine strain for the next influenza season.
Manufacturing for the next Northern Hemisphere season begins after U.S. strain selection in late February or early March.
